note: Every value below was read in this session from sources listed in research/sources.json (fetched copies under research/raw/). Anything not verifiable is marked 'pending' and must not be shown as a claim. Units: kcal/day unless stated.

nasem2023_eer.units: kcal/day; age = years; height = cm; weight = kg

6mo-2.99y.female: EER = -69.15 + (80.0 x age) + (2.65 x height) + (54.15 x weight) + growth_energy (20 kcal/d for 6-11.99mo; 15 kcal/d for 12-35.99mo)

male.inactive: EER = -447.51 + (3.68 x age) + (13.01 x height) + (13.15 x weight) + growth_energy
male.low_active: EER = 19.12 + (3.68 x age) + (8.62 x height) + (20.28 x weight) + growth_energy
male.active: EER = -388.19 + (3.68 x age) + (12.66 x height) + (20.46 x weight) + growth_energy
male.very_active: EER = -671.75 + (3.68 x age) + (15.38 x height) + (23.25 x weight) + growth_energy

female.inactive: EER = 55.59 - (22.25 x age) + (8.43 x height) + (17.07 x weight) + growth_energy
female.low_active: EER = -297.54 - (22.25 x age) + (12.77 x height) + (14.73 x weight) + growth_energy
female.active: EER = -189.55 - (22.25 x age) + (11.74 x height) + (18.34 x weight) + growth_energy
female.very_active: EER = -709.59 - (22.25 x age) + (18.22 x height) + (14.25 x weight) + growth_energy

nasem2023_eer.note: Table S-2 (Summary Table of EER Equations by Age, Sex, Physical Activity, and Energy Cost of Growth). The energy cost of growth is already included through the addend term.

pal_columns: PAL high: 1.8 (<=9y) / 2.0 (10+y) - relabelled in round-1 audit

efsa2013_ar.note: EFSA sets no AR below month 7 (assumes breastfeeding); the calculator uses PZH 2024 month-6 values (597/549) and anchors month 12 to the children year-1 AR; fractional months are interpolated (round-1 audit F2/F4). REE via Henry (2005); growth adjustment x1.01 for children.

infants_monthly_kcal_per_day.note: girls 11-12mo = 712 filled in round-1 audit (value located in the fetched copy).

tee_equations.girls_children_MJ_per_day: TEE = 1.102 + 0.273 x weight(kg) - 0.0019 x weight^2 (present in the fetched fao_y5686e06.htm; calculator reads the girls table values directly)

fao2004.catchup_energy_cost: 21 kJ (5 kcal) per gram of tissue to be laid down (Fomon 1971; Ashworth 1969; Kerr 1973; Whitehead 1973; Spady 1976; Krieger & Whitten 1976), ch. 4.
fao2004.note: Children's tables: quadratic regression on weight + energy deposition (Eg) allowance.

pzh2024.note: Polish 2024 norms; infants table equals EFSA ARs. Children tables give kcal at PAL columns.

schofield_1985_weight_height.note: As published in EFSA 2013 Appendix 13 (Schofield 1985), kcal/day; BM = body mass kg; H = height m. Krick's original method used BSA-based BMR; using these equations is a documented deviation.

henry_2005_weight_height.note: EFSA Appendix 13 (Henry 2005), kcal/day; used by EFSA for children's ARs.

equations_kcal_per_day.boys_3_10y: REE = 15.1 x BM + 74.2 x H + 306 (source flags possible kcal typo; MJ form safer)

krick_method.formula: kcal/day = (BMR x muscle_tone_factor x activity_factor) + growth_factor
krick_method.note: Factors as tabulated in Sullivan 2009 Table 1 (citing Krick et al. 1992). Original Krick BMR = BSA(m2) x standard metabolic rate (kcal/m2/h) x 24h; our calculator substitutes Schofield weight+height BMR (documented deviation).

height_based_kcal_per_cm.gate: expose only for age >= 12 months; derivation in infants unclear. Mapping of motor categories to Culley values is assumption-grade: primary text not retrieved; values read via Sullivan 2009 Table 1 / Hauer 2017 (labelled in the UI).

fluids.note: Maintenance water for parenteral/enteral fluid planning.

protein_energy_needs_table38.comment: WHO/FAO/UNU 2007 TRS 935 Table 38: protein and energy needs for catch-up growth at different rates of weight gain (typical composition 73:27 lean:fat / high-fat 50:50).

catchup.rate_limits: up to ~20x normal gain under optimal clinical conditions; realistically 2-3x normal at community level (FAO 2004 ch.4).

protein.note: TRS 935 Table 47 (safe levels; based on WHO reference weights). Catch-up protein: see catchup.protein_energy_needs_table38.

refeeding.aspn_diagnostic_criteria: decrease in any of serum phosphorus, potassium, magnesium by 10-20% (mild) / 20-30% (moderate) / >30% and/or organ dysfunction or thiamin deficiency (severe), within 5 days of reintroducing calories.
refeeding.risk_flag: WHS-chart-relative screen (user direction 2026-10-02): flag when the child's weight is approximately < -3 SD below the digitized WHS chart (Antonius 2008) using the same-side SD model; weight-for-length via the length-matched age on the WHS mean-length curve; fallback weight-for-age on the same chart when length is missing. The WHO/UNICEF SAM definition (who_sam_2009, 6-60 months) is retained as background for refeeding-risk populations but is NOT used for the screen - WHS children are constitutionally small and the WHO threshold over-flagged them.
refeeding.faltering_weight_definition: AAP/NASPGHAN 2026: weight-for-length or BMI-for-age < -1.65 z; or weight-gain velocity < -2 z (<2y); or decline >= 1 z.

nice_ng75_centile_spaces: fall across 1+ weight centile space if birthweight < 9th centile
fall across 2+ centile spaces if birthweight 9th-91st
fall across 3+ centile spaces if birthweight > 91st
current weight below 2nd centile for age (any birthweight)
safety_thresholds.note: centile space = space between adjacent centile lines (UK-WHO charts)

d2_guardrail_kcal_per_kg.note: TRS 935 Table 38 upper value for the 73:27 lean:fat column; used for the D-1/D-2 per-kg banners (50:50-fat column reaches 205).
